name: Curcumin
aliases: E100, E100(i), INS 100, INS 100(i), curcumin, curcumins, curcuma extract, turmeric extract, Curcuma longa, curcumina, curcumine, Kurkumin
what_is: Curcumin is the natural yellow pigment obtained from turmeric. In food it is used mainly as a colouring, and on a label it may appear as curcumin or E100.
why_botia: In a trial with 93 postmenopausal women, taking 500 mg of curcumin a day for eight weeks reduced hot flushes; vitamin E, the other arm of the trial, reduced them too. Anxiety, sexual function and overall symptoms did not change. The trial used 500 mg capsules; as a colouring, E100 is present in far smaller amounts, and the label does not say how much.
can_1: Detect E100, curcumin and curcuma or turmeric extract when they are declared on the label.
can_2: Explain what the clinical trial found and show the Woman and E-number information layers.
cannot_1: Determine how much curcumin a food contains, or whether it matches the dose used in the trial.
cannot_2: Tell anyone whether to take curcumin, or replace advice from a doctor.

sources.label: RCT: curcumin vs vitamin E for hot flushes in postmenopausal women (2015)
